points.point: ECB's projections put euro-area inflation at 1.4% for next year
points.quote: the ECB's projections put inflation at 1.4% for next year, which is good, but not close enough to 2%
paraphrases: ECB sees inflation at 1.4% next year
ECB's forecast puts next year's inflation at 1.4%
Euro-area inflation projected at 1.4% for next year
decoys: ECB sees inflation at 2.4% next year
ECB sees inflation reaching 2% next year

points.point: That 1.4% projection is still short of the ECB's ~2% inflation goal
patterns: (?:not close (?:enough )?to|short of|below|under|shy of|still below).{0,80}(?<!\d)2(?!\d)\s*%|(?<!\d)2(?!\d)\s*%.{0,80}(?:not close (?:enough )?to|short of|below|under|shy of|still below)
points.quote: the ECB's projections put inflation at 1.4% for next year, which is good, but not close enough to 2%
paraphrases: That's still short of the ECB's roughly 2% inflation target
1.4% remains below the ECB's near-2% goal
Inflation is projected to fall short of the ECB's ~2% objective next year
decoys: Inflation is now projected to hit the ECB's 2% target next year
The 1.4% forecast already exceeds the ECB's 2% goal

points.point: Governing Council tweaked its guidance to drop the pledge to increase the scale of monthly asset purchases, a small step toward ending QE
points.quote: the decision taken by the ECB's Governing Council last week, which entails changing our communication very slightly to show that we no longer intend to increase the scale of the central bank's monthly asset purchases
paraphrases: ECB Governing Council dropped its pledge to potentially increase QE purchases if needed
ECB tweaks guidance: no longer signals it could ramp up monthly bond buying
Governing Council removes reference to expanding asset purchases, a small step toward tapering
decoys: ECB Governing Council decided to increase the scale of its monthly asset purchases
ECB Governing Council raised interest rates for the first time since the crisis

points.point: About 0.5 percentage points of the euro area's 2.5% growth rate is attributable to ECB monetary policy
points.quote: with a growth rate of around 2.5% in the euro area, 0.5%, half a percentage point, is dependent on monetary policy
paraphrases: ECB estimates monetary policy is adding about 0.5pp to euro-area growth, without it growth would be 2% instead of 2.5%
Half a percentage point of the euro area's 2.5% growth is due to ECB measures, Cœuré says
Without the ECB's monetary stimulus, growth would be 2% rather than 2.5%, per Cœuré's estimate of a 0.5-point boost
decoys: Without ECB's measures, euro-area growth would be 3%, not 2.5%
Cœuré says growth would be unaffected by the absence of its monetary measures

points.point: Governing Council has not discussed raising rates; short-term ECB-controlled rates seen staying very low well beyond the horizon of asset purchases
patterns: (short-term (?:interest )?rates?|borrowing costs).{0,100}(very low|ultra-low|remain(?:s|ing)? low|stay(?:ing)? low)|(very low|ultra-low|remain(?:s|ing)? low|stay(?:ing)? low).{0,100}(short-term (?:interest )?rates?|borrowing costs)
points.quote: It is very clear to us that short-term interest rates those the ECB controls, will remain at very low levels, well beyond the horizon of our asset purchases
paraphrases: Cœuré: ECB-controlled short-term rates will stay very low well beyond the end of QE
Short-term rates seen anchored at ultra-low levels long after asset purchases wind down
ECB signals borrowing costs will remain very low for an extended period beyond the QE horizon
decoys: Cœuré signals short-term rates could rise as soon as asset purchases end
ECB says short-term rates will remain low only until mid-2018

points.point: End of QE is inevitable, but the Governing Council has not yet discussed the timing or manner of its termination
not_patterns: continue indefinitely|no end in sight|open-ended|will not end
points.quote: No, the end is inevitable. We have always said that quantitative easing would not last forever. We have not yet discussed the when and how of its termination.
paraphrases: Cœuré: QE will definitely end, but the ECB hasn't yet decided the timing or manner of exit
End of asset purchases is inevitable, though the 'when and how' remain undecided, says Cœuré
ECB confirms QE won't last forever but has not settled on an end date or process
decoys: Cœuré says QE will continue indefinitely with no end in sight
ECB has already agreed on the exact date to end QE

points.point: Cœuré calls a Trump-driven trade war, targeting Europe/Germany first, the major risk facing the euro area

points.quote: Europe as a whole, the euro area, and Germany in particular, was the first target of the trade war that Donald Trump wants to unleash
paraphrases: Cœuré flags a Trump trade war targeting Europe and Germany as the top risk to the euro area
ECB's Cœuré: threat of US trade war, hitting Germany hardest, is the major risk right now

decoys: Cœuré says a US trade war poses little risk to the euro area

points.point: French government debt stands at 97% of GDP; holding the deficit at 3% risks serious debt-sustainability problems
points.quote: Government debt is 97% of GDP. If our deficit remains at 3%, it is clear that we are heading towards serious debt sustainability problems.
paraphrases: Cœuré notes French government debt stands at 97% of GDP, warning that holding the deficit at 3% risks debt-sustainability problems
France's public debt is at 97% of GDP; ECB's Cœuré warns a persistent 3% deficit would raise sustainability concerns
French debt-to-GDP is 97%, and keeping the deficit near 3% would be unsustainable, Cœuré says
decoys: France's public debt stands at 79% of GDP, Cœuré notes
Cœuré says France's debt levels pose no sustainability concerns
